'''Björn Eric Gustav Bertilsson Lüning''' (18 June 1929 – 25 September 2024)<ref>{{Cite news |title=Dödsannonser |url=https://www.svd.se/special/dodsannonser |access-date=2026-08-29 |work=Svenska Dagbladet |language=sv |issn=1101-2412}}</ref> was born in [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]] to Bertil and Julia Lüning. Lüning's professional title was [[Docent]] and [[Senior lecturer|Senior Lecturer]] in [[Organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] at [[Stockholm University]]. He was also a [[filmmaker]], botanist, and a railway preservationist.

== Chemistry ==
After graduating from high school in 1947, Lüning earned a [[Bachelor of Arts degree]] in 1955, a Licentiate of Philosophy in 1957, a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Stockholm in 1960 and became a [[docent]] (associate professor) of [[organic chemistry]] at [[Stockholm University]] in 1962. He served as a research and [[teaching assistant]] at Stockholm University from 1951 to 1960, as an assistant professor from 1960 to 1966 and as a senior [[University Lecturer|lecturer]] in organic chemistry at Stockholm University beginning in 1966. He has authored works on chemistry, particularly in organic natural product chemistry.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Björn LÜNING {{!}} Stockholm University, Stockholm {{!}} SU {{!}} Department of Organic Chemistry {{!}} Research profile |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Bjoern-Luening |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=ResearchGate |language=en}}</ref>

In 1953, Björn Lüning, alongside [[Nils Löfgren]] and Harry Hedström, isolated the [[purine]] [[nucleoside]], [[nebularine]], from [[Clitocybe nebularis]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Löfgren |first=Nils |last2=Lüning |first2=Björn |last3=Hedström |first3=Harry |last4=Burris |first4=R. H. |date=1954 |title=The Isolation of Nebularine and the Determination of its Structure. |url=http://actachemscand.ki.ku.dk/doi/10.3891/acta.chem.scand.08-0670 |journal=Acta Chemica Scandinavica |language=en |volume=8 |pages=670–680 |doi=10.3891/acta.chem.scand.08-0670 |issn=0904-213X}}</ref>

== Botany ==
Lüning was a botanical researcher who specialized  in the orchid family. He has been involved in a multi-decade chemical screening series titled ''Studies on Orchidaceae alkaloids''.{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}} His work in organic natural product chemistry established a connection between structural chemistry and structural plant biology.<ref name=":0" />

He served as the chairman of the Swedish Orchid Society and authored localized reference materials, including an analysis of Carl Linnaeus's historical transit through [[Öland|Öland's]] [[Böda]] parish. In 1969, Lüning notably introduced a rare autumn-flowering orchid variety, the [[autumn lady's-tresses]] from British botanical stock onto a site in northern Öland; the planting successfully established a stable, self-sustaining wild population that grew to several hundred plants.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Marell |first=Anders MarellTextAnders |date=2024-06-20 |title=Björn Lüning firar furstlig födelsedag när han blir 95 |url=https://www.olandsbladet.se/kultur/bjorn-luning-firar-furstlig-fodelsedag-nar-han-blir-95/ |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=Ölandsbladet |language=sv}}</ref>

== Film and art ==
Lüning was an early proponent of the mid-century Swedish avant-garde film movement. Between 1946 and 1953, he experimented with 9.5mm and 16mm film formats, operating alongside the Svensk Experimentfilmstudio (later known as Arbetsgruppen för Film) in Stockholm.{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}} Lüning approached the moving image as a rhythmic medium designed to interact with music and poetry, rather than traditional narrative storytelling. His cinematic work from this period was screened withing networks of contemporary Swedish independent filmmakers.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Filmform – Björn Lüning |url=https://www.filmform.com/artists/1248-bjorn-luning/ |access-date=2026-08-29 |website=filmform.com}}</ref>

Lüning's filmography and historical biographical timeline are formally archived by Filmform, the Swedish Art Film and Video Archive. His experimental short films continue{{Failed verification|date=September 2026}} to be screened internationally in retrospectives focusing on early European vanguard cinema.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Optische Rhythmen |url=https://doi.org/10.17658/issn.2058-5462/issue-15/nead-wyver/p8 |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=doi.org}}</ref>

== Railway preservation ==
Lüning was a dedicated railway enthusiast. He acquired the historic steam locomotive, Karolina. Lüning's private collection helped spur the creation of the Sollentuna Enskilda Järnväg (SEJ) and his locomotive was loaned out to preserve the Böda Forest Railway museum line on Öland.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-19 |title=25 år sedan sista turen med den lokala järnvägen i Viby |url=https://www.mitti.se/nyheter/25-ar-sedan-sista-turen-med-den-lokala-jarnvagen-i-viby-6.27.12045.96a98c13fd |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=www.mitti.se |language=sv}}</ref>
